assumptions: Only latest two completed same-direction segments enter the raw pool.
Nearest raw segment price prerequisite and strict current price/DIF pair qualification unchanged.
Strongest eligible reference chosen, nearest first in equal-DIF ties.
Dominance only removes histories from new selection; it does not mutate locked current reference, counters or sign-flip lifecycle.
argument: The nearest completed segment cannot be dominated by a later completed same-direction segment, because no such segment exists yet.
Only the older of the two can be removed. Its possible dominating later segment is necessarily the nearest one.
The nearest-price gate already makes the current price qualify against that nearest segment. If the older DIF qualifies and is dominated, the nearest DIF is at least as extreme and qualifies too.

The unchanged strongest selection therefore chooses the nearest segment before and after removing the older one; equal-DIF ties also choose nearest. If the older one does not qualify, removing it cannot affect selection.

Identical new selection and identical locked-reference transition rules imply identical complete replay by induction over bars. The normalized sign argument applies to top and bottom directions within these candidate definitions, not to any unobserved author formula.
dominated2_logical_redundancy.limits: Does not establish crossed2 equivalence for every valid MACD sequence, more-than-two pools, a different nearest-price prerequisite, dynamic retargeting or other qualification rules.
